_comment: Game terms players can look up: tap an underlined term in card text, long-press a piece on the board, or open Menu > Glossary. 'aliases' are the words underlined in card text (whole words, any case; each term is linked once per card). 'link': false keeps a term out of card text. 'status' and 'object' tie a term (and its icon) to an engine status type or placed-object type for the board's long-press. tools/sync_game_content.ps1 copies this file into game/data/.

terms.definition: A radiation hazard on a tile. The first character to enter it, by moving, being pushed or teleporting, takes 2 damage, and then the Leak is removed. Leaks belong to no one, can't be attacked and don't block movement or line of sight. A Leak tile isn't empty, and a Leak counts as a placed object.
A placed object with 1 HP. It blocks movement and line of sight until it's destroyed. Some Flood Survivors can move through allied Stones.
A placed object with 3 HP, made by Iset-Nara's Level 3. Allies next to it gain Shield at the start of your turn.
A placed object with HP that blocks movement and line of sight until it's destroyed.
A placed object that extends the RANGE of nearby allies. The card that makes it says by how much and how far.

Anything a card puts on a tile: Stones, Leaks, the Hidden Vault, barricades or pylons. A tile with a placed object isn't empty. Objects block line of sight unless the object says otherwise (Leaks don't).

When a character with Memory would take damage, one Memory marker is removed to prevent 1 damage, after any shield. A character holds at most 1 unless a card says otherwise (Sahu-Ren holds up to 3). Some cards spend Memory for other effects.
The next allied attack against a Marked enemy deals +1 damage, and then Marked is removed.
Prevents damage up to its value and is then used up. If a character has several shields, the newest is used first. A shield lasts as long as the card that gave it says.

When a character defeats an enemy, it takes that enemy's Ember plus any Embers the enemy was carrying. Carry them to the center tile to bank them. The first team to bank 4 wins. A carrier defeated by a Leak or another hazard loses its Embers.

The character switches sides for the rest of the match. It keeps its level, HP and carried Spirit Embers, loses Marked, and can act from its new owner's next turn. A mounted pair is charmed together. Made by Zoya Miranova's Level 3, once per match; a Hero can't be charmed.
The marked tile in the middle of the board. A character carrying Spirit Embers banks all of them when it reaches the center.

Each turn you get 4 AP (on the match's first turn, the first player gets 2). Moving, attacking and using an ability each cost 1 AP. Each character also has its own character AP, usually 1, so most characters act once per turn.
Always on. A Passive ability costs no AP.
An ability you use as an action. It costs 1 AP and that character's AP.
Can be used one time in the whole match. Once-per-match Level 3 abilities cost 1 AP.
Every character starts at Level 1. A character reaches Level 2 when it gets to the opponent's back row, and Level 3 when it defeats an enemy at Level 2. Each level-up restores full HP.

A Hero or Leader can mount an adjacent allied Mount for free. The pair moves with the Mount's MOVE and AP but attacks and uses abilities with the rider's stats. Damage hits the rider, and if the rider is defeated, so is the Mount. Dismounting costs 1 AP.
Ranged attacks and abilities can't pass through a tile with a character or a placed object on it unless a card says they can.

If your Hero, or the mounted pair carrying it, has no legal move at the end of your own turn, it's captured and you lose. A Hero reduced to 0 HP is defeated like any other character, but that alone doesn't end the match.
How much damage a character can take before it's defeated.
The damage a basic attack deals.
How many tiles a character can move in one action, in a straight line.
How many tiles away a basic attack can reach, in a straight line, with line of sight.
A command piece that strengthens your other characters. A side fields only 1. It can ride a Mount.
Your most important piece. If it's trapped with no legal move at the end of your turn, you lose (Hero capture). A side fields only 1. It can ride a Mount.
A fast piece for flanking and repositioning. A Hero or Leader can ride it as a mounted pair.
A utility piece with unique rules: placing objects, swapping positions and reshaping the board.
A core combat piece built for reliable attacks and frontline pressure.
A basic piece, good for blocking and setting up plays.
A magic and support piece: curses, blessings, protection and moving other characters.
A temporary bonus to this character's attack damage. It lasts as long as the card that gave it says (usually this turn).
A temporary change to this character's MOVE.
A temporary bonus to this character's attack RANGE.
A temporary bonus to the RANGE of this character's abilities.
This character's MOVE is reduced until the effect ends.
This character can't mount or dismount until the effect ends.
This character can't be pushed, pulled or otherwise moved by enemy effects until the effect ends.
This character can't use reaction or bonus-movement effects until the effect ends.
This character may use another character's RANGE for its abilities this turn.
This character may ignore one allied character when checking line of sight this turn.
This character's next attack after moving deals +2 damage.
